body.content: Speculative fragment: on 3-regular graphs, absorbing mixed states = colorings where disagreeing edges form a matching AND each color class induces min-degree ≥ 2? Check: if a vertex has 3 same-color neighbors it has degree 3 in its color class; if it has 2, degree 2. So each color class induces min degree ≥ 2 exactly. But wait — a vertex could have only 1 same-color neighbor and 2 disagreeing: then it flips. So stability ⟺ min degree 2 in color class. On 3-regular graph, color classes have induced average degree ≥ 2 each; total edges n·3/2; two classes each with min degree 2 on sizes k and n-k: need ≥ k and ≥ n-k internal edges summing to ≤ 1.5n, always feasible. Cross edges = 1.5n - (internal), and each vertex has exactly 3 - deg_int cross edges... but stability requires deg_int ≥ 2 so cross-degree ≤ 1: disagreeing edges form a matching. Consistent.
body.possible_next_move: Compute, via simulation on random 3-regular graphs, the empirical consensus probability for n up to 10^5 and the per-vertex density of final dissenting pairs; check whether it converges to a constant and estimate ρ.
body.why_keep_this: The min-degree-2 reformulation turns the obstruction question into a clean extremal/structural question about induced subgraphs of random 3-regular graphs.
